title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
prompt:
Given an unsorted array, return the length of the longest run of **consecutive integers** (e.g. 1,2,3,4). Must run in O(n) — so no sorting.

**Example**: `[100,4,200,1,3,2]` → `4` (the run 1,2,3,4).

**Constraints**: `0 <= nums.length <= 10^5`, `-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`.
hints: Sorting would make this easy but costs O(n log n). If you could instantly ask "is x + 1 in the array?", how would you measure a run — and which numbers are worth starting from?
Put every number in a HashSet. Only count a run from its smallest element, walking x+1, x+2, … while they exist.
`x` is a run start exactly when `!set.contains(x - 1)` — skip every other x, and the total walking across all runs is O(n).

solution.explanation: Insight: with O(1) membership tests, a run can be measured by walking upward from its first element. The `x - 1` guard means each run is walked once, from its smallest value, so its length is counted correctly and no element is revisited from a non-start. Iterating the set (not the array) also ignores duplicates. O(n) time, O(n) space.
